title: Post-launch 30/60/90 KPI telemetry and rollback playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operator-friendly playbook for the first 90 days after a go-live window for features that affect model serving (hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments). It combines telemetry to watch, ownership, frequency, clear degradation thresholds, and safe rollback criteria. This doc is intended for Product Ops, SRE, Observability, and solutions-eng teams.

Scenarios covered:
- Internal beta -> early-access -> controlled ramp -> open availability
- Canary vs slow-roll vs batch release
- Model variant swaps (quantized vs float) and fallback routing to cheaper models

High-level run cadence (30/60/90):
- Day 0 (go-live): activation checklist + 4-hour rapid cadence (Console, Slack bridge).
- Days 1-3: Real-time monitoring, hourly ops stand, immediate mitigation for major regressions.
- Days 4-30: Daily KPI digest, twice-daily oncall sync for first week, then daily for weeks 2-4.
- Days 31-60: KPI trending and customer impact review weekly; focus on optimization (batching, caching) and cost signal tuning.
- Days 61-90: Readiness to graduate from pilot: final SLO verification, scale stress test, adoption handoff.

Primary KPI buckets (what to watch and why):
- Latency & Availability:
  - p50/p95/p99 generation latency (ms) — owner: SRE (Ravi Patel). Thresholds: p95 > 400ms (alpha); p99 > 900ms (amber) -> immediate triage.
  - error rate (5xx + model runtime errors) — owner: infra (Laura Kim). Thresholds: >0.5% sustained over 10m -> page.
  - request timeouts and retries — owner: product-ops (Ava Chen). >0.2% increase vs baseline -> investigate.

- Throughput & Capacity:
  - requests/sec and tokens/sec per model variant — owner: platform (Diego Morales). Track shard saturation and queue length.
  - GPU utilization and memory OOM events — owner: infra (Laura Kim). Sustained >85% GPU util -> plan scaling or throttling.

- Cost & Efficiency:
  - cost per 1k tokens and cost per request — owner: product-ops (Ava Chen). 10%+ deviation from forecast -> alert to finance cadence.
  - batching rate & average tokens per batch — owner: runtime-eng (Priya Singh). Low batch rates during high traffic -> optimization priority.

- Quality & Regression:
  - model quality signals: eval set pass-rate, hallucination rate, and rerank score drift — owner: applied-ml (Maya Lopez). Any regression flagged by eval harness -> freeze rollout.
  - customer quality feedback (support tickets tagged with model-regression) — owner: customer-success.

- Operational Signals:
  - KV/prefix cache hit rate — owner: runtime-eng. Drop below 60% -> investigate prefix alignment.
  - routing fallback frequency (requests routed to fallback model) — owner: routing-team. >2% sustained -> escalate.

Alerting & thresholds (practical triggers):
- Severity P0 (page):
  - Error rate > 2% for 2 consecutive 1m windows OR total 5xx traffic causing customer-facing outages.
  - p99 latency > 2s AND increase >2x baseline.
  - OOMs causing restarts on >3 hosts in 5 minutes.
- Severity P1 (slack + ticket):
  - p95 latency > 900ms for >10 minutes.
  - Cost per 1k tokens spikes >25% vs forecast in rolling 30m.
  - Model eval regression failing guard test on production-sampled prompts.
- Severity P2 (digest):
  - Small degradations (<10%) on non-SLO metrics, or intermittent cache hit rate drops.

Immediate mitigation playbook (first 30 minutes):
1) Triage: Confirm signal source (model variant, infra, network, client change). Reference trace/id samples.
2) If error spike or latency across model variants -> activate fallback to prior stable model and lower concurrency.
3) If GPU saturation or OOM -> reduce concurrency, shift traffic to spared region (policy permitting), or enable reserved-tier capacity.
4) If model quality regression -> pause rollout, rollback to verified model version, and mark eval regression for postmortem.
5) Communication: Post an incident summary in #prodops-launch and update the runbook doc with timestamps.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Hard rollback (immediate):
  - Any P0 condition described above.
  - Quality regression that causes customer-facing incorrect outputs at >1% of sampled requests and is reproducible.
- Soft rollback / partial rollback:
  - Sustained P1 for >15 minutes with no clear mitigation. Move to canary-only or reduce rollout velocity to 10% traffic.

Escalation ladder (who to call):
- Oncall SRE -> page first.
- Infra lead (Laura Kim) if GPU/host issues.
- Runtime/Applied ML (Priya/ Maya) for model/runtime interaction faults.
- Product PM (Diego) for customer impact and go/no-go decisions.
- VP Product Ops if >1h unresolved with active customer incidents.

Dashboards & queries (quick links and example queries to populate a daily digest):
- Primary dashboards: Latency overview, Error taxonomy, Cost burn per model, Model eval drift.
- Example metric query (pseudo-SQL/PromQL):
  - p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
  - error_rate = sum(rate(requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))
  - cost_per_k_tokens = sum(rate(token_cost_total[1m])) / (sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[1m])) / 1000)

Daily digest template (automated):
- Top-level: traffic summary (requests, tokens), overall p95/p99, error rate, cost delta vs forecast.
- Owners notes: one-line status from SRE, Infra, Applied-ML, Product-ops.
- Open items: mitigations in-flight, expected actions for next 24h.

Postmortem & learning loop (for any P0/P1 incidents during 90d):
- Timeline + root cause analysis + code/infra/pr change list.
- KPI impact table (delta vs baseline).
- Preventative actions: dashboard or alert improvements, runbook additions, automation opportunities.
- Release gating update: add any new preflight checks to the staging harness.

Graduation checklist (ready to exit pilot at day 90):
- SLOs met for 21 of the last 30 days with p99 under target for steady traffic windows.
- No unresolved P0 incidents in last 30 days.
- Cost variance within agreed budget +/- 10%.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts documented, oncall runbook readable and tested during a fire drill.
- Customer success: no critical adoption blockers, support playbook in place.

Appendix: quick templates
- Incident post to Slack (snippet):
  - [INCIDENT] short desc | impacted models | p95/p99 | current mitigation | next step | owner
- Rollback comment template for audit:
  - Rollback initiated by: <name> | time: <UTC> | reason: <primary signal> | previous model/tag: <vX.Y.Z> | follow-ups: <jira keys>

Notes & open questions (for this launch):
- Do we need an automated circuit-breaker that reduces concurrency at the edge when p95 latency crosses threshold? (SRE action item)
- Should finance be automatically paged for cost spikes above 40% (we currently only notify)
- Add a small sampling pipeline to store 0.1% of requests for model-quality re-eval without PII; confirm retention and privacy signoff.

Owners & contacts:
- Product Ops (lead) — Ava Chen (ava@redwood.ai)
- SRE — Ravi Patel (ravi@redwood.ai)
- Infra — Laura Kim (laura@redwood.ai)
- Platform/Product — Diego Morales (diego@redwood.ai)
- Runtime/Applied ML — Priya Singh (pri@redwood.ai), Maya Lopez (maya@redwood.ai)

If you are reading this while monitoring a live rollout: follow the first page run cadence, keep a single source-of-truth thread for decisions, and err on the side of rollback when both user experience and model quality are impacted.

-- end of playbook --
